clarifications: House ruling: this property is used in the book but not defined. Temporary definition.

spells.name: Heat resistance
spells.text: Character enables himself to resist heat. He can resist heat as if he was standing in a large blazing campfire, without getting damaged. When attacked by magically induced fire, he gains ‘Resistance’, equal to the intensity score selected for the spell.

spells.name: Firebolt
spells.text:
The caster flicks his hand, and a bolt of searing hot fire darts from his fingertips.
On a hit, the target must pass a Reaction save with a DC equal to the intensity of the spell, or take ‘Persistent(2): Fire’.

spells.name: Heat water
spells.text: The character can heat up an area of water. Creatures entering or starting their turn in the heated water must make a Fortitude save with a DC equal to the intensity of the spell, or suffer ‘Persistent’ fire damage equal to the points of failed save for 1 round.

spells.name: Ablaze
spells.text: Caster can ignite a number of normal combustible sources, like dry wood, a piece of cloth, a torch, a bale of hay, candles, braziers, etc. equal to the intensity rank chosen, and within the burst rank chosen. Creatures, whose cloth, skin or the likes catches fire must make a Reaction save with a DC equal to the spell caster’s HDC. The points of failure being the DMR of the heat damage.

spells.name: Ring of fire
spells.text: Character creates a ring of fire around him. Everyone entering or staying in the circle of flames, at the start of their turn, takes fire damage. Anyone taking damage from the fire, must pass a Reaction save equal to the intensity score of the spell, or suffer ‘Persistent(2)’ fire damage.

spells.name: Fireball
spells.text: An explosive ball of fire is shot from the palm of the caster, flying in a direct line at the area where it explodes, creating AoE damage. Anyone caught in the explosion must pass a Fortitude save with a DC equal to the intensity score of the spell. Any points of failure are added to the DMR of the Fireball. Also, failing the save means the target suffers a ‘Persistent(2)’ fire damage.

spells.name: Firewall
spells.text: The caster creates wall of intense fire, flaming up in a 2 meter height. Anyone entering the zone or staying in it, at the start of their turn, takes AoE-damage. Anyone taking damage from the fire, must pass a Fortitude save with a DC equal to the intensity score of the spell. Any points of failure are added to the DMR of the Firewall. Also, failing the save means the target suffers a ‘Persistent(2)’ fire damage.

spells.name: Flaming blade
spells.text: The caster can imbue flames on a number of weapons equal to the intensity rank, within the range of the Burst rank area. The weapon(s) gain a DMR bonus equal to the DMR variable, and their attacks gain the ‘Fire’ trait.

spells.name: Dual flame
spells.text:
From the outstretched hand of the caster flares two bolts of fire, enabling him to attack a single target twice or two separate targets once. This spell counts as one attack in regard to the MAP.
On a hit, the target must pass a Reaction save with a DC equal to the intensity of the spell, or take ‘Persistent(2): Fire’.

spells.name: Dragonfire
spells.text: From the outstretched arms and hands of the caster, erupts a powerful engulfing wave of dragon hot fire. Anyone taking damage from the fire, must pass a Fortitude save with a DC equal to the intensity score of the spell. Any points of failure are added to the DMR of the Dragonfire. Also, failing the save means the target suffers a ‘Persistent(2)’ fire damage.

spells.name: Heat immunity
spells.text: The caster becomes immune to fire damage, and can also withstand being in extreme hot areas like a volcano.

spells.name: Fire lance
spells.text: A massive lance of fire is launched from the hand of the caster, hammering into whatever target he directs the lance at. On a hit, the target must pass a Reaction save with a DC equal to the intensity of the spell or take ‘Persistent(4): Fire’.

spells.name: Firestorm
spells.text: The caster designates an area, where a massive storm of churning fire arises, burning everyone entering it, or starting their turn in it. Anyone taking damage from the fire, must pass a Fortitude save with a DC equal to the intensity score of the spell. Any points of failure are added to the DMR of the Firestorm. Also, failing the save means the target suffers a ‘Persistent(4)’ fire damage.

spells.name: Triad of flame
spells.text:
From the outstretched hand of the caster flares three bolts of fire, enabling him to attack a single target three times or split the three attacks at separate targets. This spell counts as one attack in regards to the MAP.
On a hit, the target must pass a Reaction save with a DC equal to the intensity of the spell, or take ‘Persistent(2): Fire’.

spells.name: Meteor
spells.text:
The caster conjures a meteor, slamming down from above, striking the target, and surrounding area for massive damage.
Anyone taking damage from the fire, must pass a Fortitude save with a DC equal to the intensity score of the spell. Any points of failure are added to the DMR of the Meteor.
Also, failing the save means the target suffers a ‘Persistent(4)’ fire damage.

spells.name: Fire rain
spells.text:
In an area, the caster summons a rain of fire, hailing down bolt of searing hot fire from above. The caster is allowed a single firebolt attack against each creature in the burst zone.
On a hit, the target must pass a Reaction save with a DC equal to the intensity of the spell, or take ‘Persistent(2): Fire’.

spells.name: Meteor shower
spells.text:
The caster can make a number of meteor attacks equal to the zone variable. The attacks must be within the blast area of the spell.
Anyone taking damage from the fire, must pass a Fortitude save with a DC equal to the intensity score of the spell. Any points of failure are added to the DMR of the Meteor strike. Also, failing the save means the target suffers a ‘Persistent(4)’ fire damage.

spells.name: Stone staff
spells.text: The caster magically conjures a staff of beautiful and ornate stone, he can use as a melee weapon and make melee attack rolls, using his Directed Spells skill. He gains a melee attack bonus equal to the intensity rating of the spell.

spells.name: Tremors
spells.text: The character stomps a single time in the ground, creating a violent shock wave, shaking the immediate area around him. Everyone caught in the burst area must pass a Reaction save vs. the intensity of the spell, or be knocked prone.

spells.name: Rock hurl
spells.text: The character can channel energy to summon rocks and pebbles from his nearby surroundings (even if they are underground), hurling them at his foes. The intensity rating defines the number of rocks in the cluster, each granting an attack roll.

spells.name: Earthwall
spells.text:
The caster summons a wall of solid, packed earth. Each space it occupies, is with 1x1x2 (WxDxH) meters. Each space wall has a number of BP equal to the caster's max, but is shattered on a critical hit. MP. The wall has a DFR of 15, and TOU of 10. Anyone attacking the wall (to hack through), must make a weapon save with 2 advantages for the used weapon. The TOU can be increased by the intensity score.
If a creature is caught in a space, where the Earthwall is summoned, they get a Reaction save. On a successful save, they manage to move to a vacant adjacent space, as a free action. On a failure, they are encased in the dirt, becoming ‘Restrained’. They can break free on their turn with a successful Fortitude save, whereas the Earthwall crumbles to the ground in that space, as if it was hacked down, even if the rest of the wall is still in effect.

spells.name: Crystal shield
spells.text:
The caster creates a crystal shield, that is extremely light, but very hard and durable. The shield functions as a normal shield, with an DFR modifier equal the intensity score. The shield occupies 1 hand, counting in any way like a shield (and enters the game raised).
Every use of the shield reduces it's DFR modifier by 1 point. When reaching zero, the shield shatters. The shield incurs no penalties to the caster.

spells.name: Earth Golem
spells.text: The caster summons a golem of compact, dense earth and pebbles. The caster can command it from the next round, as an action (the Golem then has 2 actions). The Golem's stats are: BP: Half caster's max MP; Melee skill is 4 + caster's level; DFR 10+ caster's level; TOU equals Intensity; Melee DMR equal to spell DMR; Movement rate equal to zone variable. The Golem perishes on a critical hit.

spells.name: Stoneskin
spells.text:
The caster magically imbues a target with a harder skin, enabling him to better withstand incoming damage. The target gains a bonus to DFR and TOU equal to the intensity rating.
The bonus, however, divides itself equally between DFR and TOU. Thus, a +1 goes to TOU, a +2 goes with +1 to TOU and +1 DFR, a +3 with +2 TOU and +1 DFR etc.

spells.name: Stone to earth
spells.text: The caster channels magical energies, to transform solid rock surface into dense packed earth instead. The transformed stone becomes similar to an earth wall instead. The spell can also be used to transform a magically created stone wall into an earth wall. The transformation is permanent.

spells.name: Pass through stone
spells.text:
The caster gains the ability to pass through solid stone by casting this spell. The caster can traverse through a distance of solid stone, equal to the zone variable.
Getting stuck in stone, will crush whatever body part being stuck, rendering it useless (500 RP).

spells.name: Stonewall
spells.text:
The caster summons a wall of pebbles, rocks or even minor boulders. Each space it occupies, is with 1x1x2 (WxDxH) meters. Each space wall has a number of BP equal to twice the caster's max. MP, but is shattered on a critical hit. The wall has a DFR of 20, and TOU of 20. Anyone attacking the wall (to hack through), must make a weapon save, for the used weapon. The DFR can be increased by the intensity score.
If a creature is caught in a space, where the Stonewall is summoned, they get a Reaction save. On a successful save, they manage to move to a vacant adjacent space, as a free action. On a failure, they are encased in the dirt, becoming ‘Restrained’. They can break free on their turn with a successful Fortitude save with 2 disadvantages, whereas the Stonewall crumbles to the ground in that space, as if it was hacked down, even if the rest of the wall is still in effect.

spells.name: Stone Golem
spells.text:
The caster summons a golem of pebbles, rocks and boulders. The caster can command it from the next round, as an action (the Golem then has 2 actions). The Golem's stats are:
BP: Equal to caster's max MP; Melee skill is 3 + caster's level; DFR 10+ caster's level; TOU equals Intensity; Melee DMR equal to spell DMR; Movement rate equal to zone. The Golem perishes on a critical hit.

spells.name: Crystal shards
spells.text:
Caster creates a whirling stream of razor sharp crystals, lunging them at a target.
The caster gains a number of separate attacks with his Directed Spells skill, equal to the intensity score of the spell.

spells.name: Crystal staff
spells.text: The caster magically conjures a staff of clean sparkling crystal, he can use as a melee weapon and make melee attack rolls, using his Directed Spells skill. He gains a melee attack bonus equal to the intensity rating of the spell.

spells.name: Stone bridge
spells.text: The caster can channel the elemental energies of the world. Summoning stones from the nearby area, to form in front of him, as a stone bridge. Even though the stone bridge is magically held and sustained, it must originate from a solid surface (not necessarily stone) - it cannot float midair - and will collapse into dust and gravel once the duration expires. The bridge can carry a w eight equal to 25 kg per intensity point chosen.

spells.name: Crystal golem
spells.text: The caster summons a golem of pure crystal shards. The caster can command it from the next round, as an action. The Golem's stats are: BP: Equal to twice the caster's max MP; Melee skill is 3 + caster's level; DFR 10+ caster's level; TOU equals Intensity; Melee DMR equal to spell DMR; Movement rate equal to zone. The Golem perishes on a critical hit.

spells.name: Magma golem
spells.text:
The caster summons a golem of moulding magma. The caster can command it from the next round, as an action. The Golem's stats are: BP: Equal to twice the caster's max MP; Melee skill is 3 + caster's level; DFR 10+ caster's level; TOU equals Intensity; Melee DMR equal to spell DMR; Movement rate equal to zone. The Golem perishes on a critical hit.
Anyone starting their turn adjacent to the Magma golem, must pass a Fortitude save vs.
the caster’s HDC or take damage equal to the golem’s DMR, adding any points of failed save to the DMR before rolling damage.

spells.name: Icebolt
spells.text: A cluster of freezing air and icy crystals form around the caster's hand, then launches forward as a bolt of hardened ice. If struck, the target must pass a Fortitude save, or become ‘Rooted(5)’ for 1 round.

spells.name: Waterbreathing
spells.text:
Through magical means, the caster enables himself to breath underwater. The effect of the spell doesn't offer any enhanced underwater movement or capabilities.
Caster gains a concentration save bonus equal to the intensity score.

spells.name: Find water
spells.text: By tapping into the magical streams, and interpreting the signals, the character gets a sense of nearby water sources identifying its type (saltwater, freshwater, etc.). The caster can ping a source, once discovered, and thereby travel towards it. The range is the radius in km, the spell effects spans.

spells.name: Cold resistance
spells.text:
Character enables himself to resist coldness. He can resist coldness as if he was standing in a large biting blizzard in the middle of the tundra, without taking damage.
When attacked by magically induced cold, he gains ‘Resistance(x)’ equal to the intensity rating of the spell.

spells.name: Flood
spells.text:
The caster creates a blast area with small tidal wave, flooding away from the caster.
Anyone caught in the flood must make a Fortitude save vs the intensity rating of the spell.
On a successful save, the target(s) are only knocked prone. Otherwise they are pushed back 2 meters for each 5 points of failure, and takes normal fall damage for each 2 meters (targets cannot be pushed farther than the blast range).

spells.name: Waterwalking
spells.text: The spell enables the caster to move on water. If the character needs to run, jump, fight etc., he must pass a DC10 Concentration save to sustain the ability to stay above water, each round he engages in energetic movement. The intensity rating grants bonus to any Concentration save.

spells.name: Waterwall
spells.text: The caster creates a 2 meter high wall of churning water. Each space is 1x1x2 meters (WxDxH). Passing through a space with a waterwall costs an additional action. Attacking through a waterwall is done with disadvantage. The wall furthermore offers cover, as line of sight is obscured. Staying in the wall of water is resolved like being under normal water (risk of drowning).

spells.name: Conjure water
spells.text: Caster creates a number of portions clean, cold and fresh water equal to the result of the intensity rating.

spells.name: Spear of winter
spells.text:
The caster conjures a large jagged spear of hardened and packed ice, propelling it at a single target, using the Directed spells skill.
If struck, the target must pass a Fortitude save, or become ‘Rooted(5)’ for 1 round.

spells.name: Bonechiller
spells.text: Caster sprays out a blast zone of bone chilling and frigid air. Anyone caught in the blast must pass a Fortitude save vs. the intensity rating of the spell, or take 1 damage/failure and become ‘Stunned(1)’ for each 5 points of failure.

spells.name: Icestorm
spells.text: The caster creates a zone of intensified frigid storm, filled with small sharp ice shards, darting around its interior. Anyone entering the zone or starting their turn in the zone must make a Fortitude save, adding any points of failure to the DMR of the spell, and gains the ‘Stunned(1)’ condition for each 5 points of failure.

spells.name: Icewall
spells.text: The caster summons a wall of solid, packed ice. Each space point it occupies, is done with 1x1x2 meters (WxDxH). The wall can be hacked through, and has a number of BP equal to twice caster's maximum MP. DFR of 10 and TOU of 20. The caster can increase the DFR by the intensity score. Any attacks against the wall, that does not result in a critical attack, forces a weapon save on the used weapon.

spells.name: Cold immunity
spells.text:
The character is immune to cold, and can't take damage from cold damage.
The character gains a bonus to Concentration checks equal to the intensity rating.

spells.name: Permafrost beam
spells.text:
From the outstretched hands of the caster, springs a massive and highly concentrated beam of subzero temperature, damaging everything in its wake.
The caster can mold the zone range in any straight line and thickness (e.g. an 8 meter zone can be a 4x4 meter field, or an 8x2 beam). Anyone struck by the beam must make a Fortitude save, adding any points of failure to the DMR of the spell, and gains the ‘Stunned(1)’ condition for each 5 points of failure.

spells.name: Frostspire
spells.text:
Conjured from the sky, falls a massive spire of ice, hammering to the ground, damaging everyone in the area of effect.
Anyone struck by the beam must make a Fortitude save, adding any points of failure to the DMR of the spell, and gains the ‘Stunned(1)’ condition for each 5 points of failure.

spells.name: Light
spells.text: Caster creates a source of light, originating from a point of the caster's choice. Once placed, the light remains active from this point, until it fades. The light creates a pleasant blue-white light, resembling daylight. This light cannot, illuminate magically created darkness. The light reacts like normal light, casting shadows, can be covered, etc.

spells.name: Gloom
spells.text: The caster meddles with the magical streams, distorting reality, and dimming natural light in an area, originating from a point. Bright light becomes dim light, dim light becomes darkness

spells.name: Gale
spells.text:
The caster surrounds himself with a field of extremely hefty wind whirling up debris and small objects. Anyone in the zone has disadvantage on melee attacks, due to obscured sight, as well does ranged attacks shooting into or through the chaotic wind field.
The caster can gain a concentration save bonus equal to the intensity of the spell.

spells.name: Lightning bolt
spells.text:
Character can do one of two things, either conjures a highly intense, crackling lightning bolt, darting at his target. He must make a ranged attack with the Directed Spells skill to hit.
Otherwise, he can cast it as a blast spell, considered an AoE-attack.
A target, struck by the attack, must pass a Fortitude save, or become ‘Disoriented(1)’ until the end of his next turn.

spells.name: Sunburst
spells.text: The caster taps into the magical streams, and conjures a powerful flash of bright white light. Anyone caught in the zone must make a Reaction save against the intensity rating of the spell, or become ‘Stunned(1)’ and ‘Blinded’ until the end of their next turn.

spells.name: Airpocket
spells.text:
Caster creates a sort of energy field around him, containing clean breathable air. The spheric energy field moves with the caster, enabling him to move through toxic atmospheres.
This spell cannot be used to breath under water.

spells.name: Speed
spells.text: The caster magically imbues the target with lightning speed, granting the target a speed bonus equal to the intensity rating of the spell.

spells.name: Purify air
spells.text: The caster weaves the magical streams to cleanse an area of air. The character can cleanse an area equal to a 2x2x2 meter space per intensity rating of the spell. The air becomes clean and breathable, shunning any toxins, gases, germs, bacteria, or other natural compounds (eg. does not cleanse curse).

spells.name: Chain lightning
spells.text:
From the palm of the caster jumps a beam of lightning that jumps from enemy to enemy, within reach of the range. The caster makes a Directed Spells attack against each target, with a disadvantage for each new target beyond the first.
A target, struck by the attack, must pass a Fortitude save, or become ‘Disoriented(1)’ until the end of his next turn.

spells.name: Poisonous mist
spells.text:
The caster conjures an area of sickly green and heavy mist filled with poisonous spores, lingering in the area. As the cloud is magically created, it is unaffected by wind or the natural environment. A creature starting its turn in the cloud, must pass a Fortitude save or take damage equal to the save failure and gain the 'Poisoned' condition, and doing so at the end of each of its turns, until passing the save.
A creature passing the cloud in one uninterrupted move, gains advantage to its Fortitude save.

spells.name: Jolt
spells.text: The caster permeates the target with electric currents, making the target spasm, and lock up. The target must succeed a Fortitude save vs. The intensity rating of the spell. On a fail from 1-5, the target becomes ‘Disoriented(3)’. If he fails with more than 5, he becomes ‘Stunned(3)’ instead.

spells.name: Lightning strikes
spells.text:
The caster creates a field of intense lightning strikes. He is allowed to make a number of attacks equal to the zone variable of the spell, using his Directed Spells skill. The number of attacks can be made against a single target, or spread across multiple targets within the Burst zone.
A target, struck by the attack, must pass a Fortitude save, or become ‘Disoriented(1)’ until the end of his next turn.

spells.name: Cloud dive
spells.text:
By invoking the magical streams of the Aether, the caster can cushion the impact of a fall.
The caster is allowed to reduce the number of meters fallen by the intensity rating, when determining the fall distance, and hence the damage.

spells.name: True light
spells.text: Caster creates an aura of bright, pleasant daylight in an area. The light is, in contrast to the normal light spell, a magically summoned light, and can light up magically created darkness. Moreover, within the zone of the light, no shadows are cast - everything is illuminated. This celestial light is the only source to contest 'True darkness'.

spells.name: True darkness
spells.text:
The caster manipulates the magical streams to contort reality. By doing so he creates a magical, heavy, deep darkness, that cannot be illuminated by natural light sources.
Everything within the zone becomes pitch dark.
Even creatures with darkvision, low-light vision etc. are blinded in this darkness. This foul darkness can only be contested by 'True light'.

spells.name: Healing
spells.text: A golden light emits from the caster's hands, and runs over the target, healing his wounds. The target regains 1 BP per intensity rating.

spells.name: Vigor
spells.text: The caster uses the power of the Aether to imbue a target with vital energies, granting him an almost supernatural fountain of life. The target gains a number of temporary BP equal to the intensity rating of the spell. The temporary BP can extend beyond the target's normal BP maximum.

spells.name: Fortify
spells.text: The caster incantates, creating a greenish shimmering light, engulfing the target, magically reinforcing the toughness (TOU), by the intensity rating.

spells.name: Bloodstop
spells.text: The caster can magically stop blood from gushing, and close the wound of the target. The amount of bleed points this spell can reduce, is equal to the intensity score. Once healed, the bleed effect is removed.

spells.name: Shield
spells.text:
The caster creates a protective aura around the target, causing incoming attacks to be slightly blocked or deflected.
The target gains a DFR bonus equal to the intensity rating of the spells.

spells.name: Cure disease
spells.text: Through magical means, the caster jolts and empowers the natural resistance of the target. The target is allowed to make an immediate save vs. A single disease affecting his system, with a save bonus equal to the intensity score of the spell.

spells.name: Deflection
spells.text:
The caster creates an immediate burst of deflective energy force in front of the target, causing the attack of an enemy to bend off just as it would otherwise have struck.
The target gains an immediate DFR bonus against a single attack, equal to the intensity rating.

spells.name: Rejuvenate the dying
spells.text: With this spell, the caster can channel magical energies into the target(s), that interrupts the dying state, returning the target to a state of unconsciousness instead.

spells.name: Pain tolerance
spells.text: The caster imbues the target(s) with a tolerance to pain. Increasing their resistance to ‘Stunned’ conditions from attacks. The number of ‘Stunned’ effects the target can absorb is equal to the intensity rating. If the target is subjected to a ‘Stunned’ condition afterwards, the spell absorbs it, leaving no effect. If an attack results in multiple stuns, the spell negates as many as it can instantly.

spells.name: Mending
spells.text: The caster uses the magic of the Aether, to immensely speed up the natural recovery of a wound. The caster can heal 1 instance of the ‘Wounded’ condition per point of intensity rating.

spells.name: Cure poison
spells.text: Through magical means, the caster jolts and empowers the natural resistance of the target. The target is allowed to make an immediate save vs. A single poison affecting his system, with a save bonus equal to the intensity score of the spell.

spells.name: Healing wave
spells.text: The caster emits a burst of soothing energy. All allies within the burst regains 1 BP per point of intensity rating.

spells.name: Faith
spells.text: The caster sends out an encouraging aura of positive magical energy, enforcing close allies with improved faith. All allies in range gains advantage to all saves while they are within range of the aura.

spells.name: Aura of inspiration
spells.text: The caster creates an aura around him, imbuing his closest allies with magical inspiration. Each ally within range of the aura, gains advantage to skill checks (including combat and spell casting).

spells.name: Regeneration
spells.text:
The caster magically imbues a target with the ability to regenerate superficial injury.
Once affected, the target heals a number of BP equal to the intensity score each minute, for the duration of the spell. It still lingers if the target should fall unconscious while effected, but not if totally killed.

spells.name: Awaken
spells.text: The caster magically contacts an unconscious target, jolting his consciousness, awakening him from his passive state. The target awakes with 1 BP. All injuries, effects and ailments are not healed by this spell.

spells.name: Sphere of protection
spells.text: The caster can instantaneously create a sphere of forceful energy, partially disrupting the effect of harmful elements. Each harmful element passing through the sphere, will have its damage reduced by the intensity rating of this spell. However, damage dealt within the confines of the sphere is not affected.

spells.name: Cure curse
spells.text: Through magical means, the caster jolts and empowers the natural resistance of the target. The target is allowed to make an immediate save vs. A single curse affecting his system, with a save bonus equal to the intensity score of the spell.

spells.name: Bolster
spells.text:
The caster sends out an aura of empowering energy, hardening his close allies.
Every ally within range of the Burst, gain a bonus to their TOU equal to the intensity rating.

spells.name: Protection
spells.text:
The caster sends out an aura of protective energy, warding his close allies.
Every ally within range of the Burst, gain a bonus to their DFR equal to the intensity rating.

spells.name: Arise
spells.text: The caster magically contacts an unconscious target, jolting his consciousness, awakening him from his passive state. The target awakes with 25 BP. All injuries, effects and ailments are not healed by this spell.

spells.name: Immune to disease
spells.text: Through manipulation of the Aether, the caster strengthens his target to become immune to any disease, including magically inflicted diseases. The spell does not cure, however, any diseases affecting the target before the spell is cast.

spells.name: Immune to poison
spells.text: Through manipulation of the Aether, the caster strengthens his target to become immune to any poison, including magically inflicted poisons. The spell does not cure, however, any poisons affecting the target before the spell is cast.

spells.name: Immune to curse
spells.text: Through manipulation of the Aether, the caster strengthens his target to become immune to any curses, including magically inflicted curses. The spell does not cure, however, any curses affecting the target before the spell is cast.

spells.name: Resilience
spells.text: The caster grants the target close to immortal state, by granting him resistance to any type of damage equal to the intensity rating of the spell.

spells.name: Revive
spells.text:
The caster channels great amounts of Aether, to bring back a creature from the dead.
The spell can only work however, if the creature's spirit has not lefts its body.

spells.name: Communicate with animals
spells.text:
When casting this spell, the caster gains the ability to communicate telepathically with a selected type of animal (insects, spinners, canine, feline, amphibians, fish, etc.). If the caster wishes to communicate with another type of animal, he must cast the spell anew.
If the target(s) are unwilling, they are allowed a Willpower save vs. the spells Intensity rating.

spells.name: Restoration
spells.text: A soothing greenish light emits from the caster's hands, running over the target, healing his wounds. The target regains a number of BP equal to the intensity score of the spell.

spells.name: Communicate with plants
spells.text: By casting this spell, the caster gains the ability to communicate with plants and vegetation. The caster must choose a type of plant (Tree, bushes, grass, corals, seaweed, flowers, etc.). If the target(s) are unwilling, they are allowed a Willpower save vs. the spells Intensity rating.

spells.name: Wildtooth
spells.text: The caster conjures and lunges a bolt of sharpened hard wood at his target, allowing him to make a Directed spells attack against the target.

spells.name: Tentacle roots
spells.text:
With this spell, the caster summons roots and vines, to entangle and grapple the target(s). Each target must make a Fortitude save vs the spell's Intensity rating, or become ‘Immobilized’ and ‘Constrained where they stand, as roots and vines encase them in an organic shell.
A target can use an action to make a new Fortitude save vs. the intensity to get escape.
The area counts as difficult terrain.

spells.name: Low-light vision
spells.text: Character imbues himself with magical power from the Aether, enabling him to gain low- light vision within the range of the burst distance.

spells.name: Find water
spells.text: The caster tunes in on the magical streams in the world, isolating himself from the world for a moment, and listens to the language of magic. By sending out this pulse, he can feel where the closes drinkable (without becoming sick, infected, contaminated, etc.) water source is.

spells.name: Shelter
spells.text: Using the Aether, the caster attunes to nature, calming the area around him and his campsite. The increased tranquility of the environment means, all allies within the burst range gains an additional number of recovery points equal to the intensity rating of the spell, when all have finished a long rest.

spells.name: Wilderness staff
spells.text: The caster creates a wonderful staff of natural design, with which he has such a magical attunement that he can make melee attacks with it, by using his Directed Spells skill for the melee attack checks.

spells.name: Find herbs
spells.text: The caster tunes in on the magical streams in the world, isolating himself from the world for a moment, and listens to the language of magic. By sending out this pulse, he can feel, where the closes source of herbs. Each herb being mentally indscribed into a sort of mindmap, enabling him to ping them and find them.

spells.name: Fangs of the forest
spells.text: The character conjures a solid, pointy, straight spear-like staff of hardened wood and darts it at his foe. The caster can create a number of spears equal to the intensity rating, gaining an attack per spear created, each rolled for individually. Each spear will have the same assigned damage rating.

spells.name: Elemental resistance
spells.text: By utilizing the energy from the magical streams, the caster bolsters himself against the four elements. Gaining ‘Resistance’ equal to the intensity rating, against any harmful elements that rises from the four core elements: Earth, Fire, Water and Air.

spells.name: Water breathing
spells.text:
With this spell, the caster is able to breathe as well under water, as above water.
However, the water breathing capacity does not protect him from ingesting contaminated water, infectious or germ-infested particles floating around in the water.
Even though he CAN breathe under the surface, other harmful elements from or in the water still affect him. This spell does also not grant him any increased underwater movement capabilities.

spells.name: Field of thorns
spells.text: As the caster channels the magical energies, a field of black, sturdy and magical briar thorn shoots up from the ground. In almost an instant, the spiked roots and branches curl and twist, creating a seemingly impassable area. The spell can be a ranged burst, or a blast type spell. For each movement action taken in this area the target must make a Fortitude save vs. the intensity rating of the spell, and take damage equal to each point of failure. The field is also considered difficult terrain.

spells.name: Darkvision
spells.text: When the caster activates this spell, he gains perfect darkvision, enabling him to see in pitch darkness. This sight doesn't allow to distinguish colors, temperature etc., as the sight only allows nuances and variances from black, through grey, to white. This spell does not enable the character to see in True Darkness.

spells.name: Hawkeye
spells.text: On activation of this spell, the character gains an incredible boost of eyesight. Enabling him to see a lot farther, distinguishing fine and subtle details like personal characteristics, embroidery, coat of arms, etc. It does not, however, come with an increase sense of hand-eye coordination, and thus no bonusses to shooting, etc. applies.

spells.name: Acute senses
spells.text: Through the channels of the magical streams, the caster is able to tune one or more senses to better perceive what is going on around him. The caster can choose a sense for each point of Intensity score. Each point granting an advantage to ‘Perception & Awareness’ checks.

spells.name: Refuge
spells.text: While camped, the caster can put up a magical veil of guile, dampening sound and sight, making it harder to locate the campsite. Any creature getting close enough to locate the campsite naturally, but still outside the Burst of the spell, must pass a ‘Perception & Awareness’ check vs. the intensity rating of the spell to notice the camp.

spells.name: Detect living
spells.text: By channeling the magical streams, the caster can send out a sort of magical sonic wave, enabling him to ping and feel every living creature in the area. Giving him an understanding of their whereabouts. Also allowing him to briefly notice their silhouette as a faint blue-grey luminescence, for the duration of the spell. This spell does not, however, grant him any insight into their demeanor, mental state, intensions or condition.

spells.name: Druid staff
spells.text: The caster creates a wonderful staff of impressive and natural design, with which he has such a magical attunement that he can make melee attacks with it, by using his Directed Spells skill for the melee attack checks.

spells.name: Shared senses
spells.text: The caster connects with an animal, to share all of it's senses. He does not exert any control over the animal. He must be able to see it, once the spell is cast, but afterwards it can leave line of sight, without breaking the connection. This also works with animals the caster has detected or senses through other spells, even without line of sight. This spell also enables him to get a read on the animal's general condition and it's emotional state.

spells.name: Thermal vision
spells.text: By manipulating the magical streams, the caster is able to turn his sight into a thermal vision, and by so, able to see and navigate through color distinction due to heat signatures created by creatures and the environment.

spells.name: Merge with nature
spells.text: This spell allows the caster to blend with nature. Transforming himself, to merge with any organic material like bushes, trees, grass, etc. It does not cover merging with inorganic materials like stone, metal and the likes. The caster must be in physical contact with the item he wants to merge with. The transformation is so life-like that only detection of magic will reveal him. He can, however, take damage.

spells.name: Merge with inanimate
spells.text: With this spell, the caster can merge with inanimate objects like stone or metal. Not in the sense he can pass through it, or move around it, but he will look like a perfectly natural extension of the inanimate material he touches. The transformation is so life-like, only detection of magic will reveal him. He can, however, take damage.

spells.name: Elemental immunity
spells.text: By utilizing the energy from the magical streams, the caster bolsters himself against the four elements. Gaining immunity, against any harmful exposure, arising from the four core elements: Earth, Fire, Water and Air.

spells.name: Gift of nature
spells.text: The caster creates a wonderful staff of marvelous and natural design, with which he has such a magical attunement that he can make melee attacks with it, by using his Directed Spells skill for the melee attack checks.

spells.name: Telekinesis
spells.text: The caster can move items up to 10 kg. per point of Zone variable. The item is moved at a speed equal to the range per combat round. Any attempt to obstruct the telekinetic movement, must be done with a check against the intensity rating.

spells.name: Read person
spells.text:
The caster reads the essence of a person. Gaining insight into one piece information pr.
point of the zone variable: Level, archetype, demeanor, motivations, alignment, etc.
Unwilling target must pass a Willpower save vs. the intensity of the spell, to avoid the reading.

spells.name: Blink
spells.text:
This spell allows the caster to teleport very short distances. Immediately disappearing in one place, to reappear in another. The caster must be able to see the point of destination.
He is able to teleport a number of meters equal the zone variable. Leaving an adjacent enemy this way, does not provoke reactive actions.

spells.name: Power jump
spells.text: The caster magically thrust himself through the air, enabling him to jump a number of meters equal to the zone variable. This spell adds no additional air control, while being midair. However, landing safely is part of the effect, assuming it is a fairly straight forward jump. Being interrupted midair, or trying to make acrobatic maneuvers, while in the air may result in landing failure. The caster can add an ‘Athletics & Acrobatics’ bonus equal to the Intensity rating.

spells.name: Landing
spells.text: The caster slows down or negates a fall or drop with his magical powers. The caster is able to reduce the effect of the fall distance in meters, equal to the range variable. The spell does not include air control, change of direction or acrobatic maneuvers.

spells.name: Aether thrust
spells.text: Everyone in the blast zone must make a Fortitude save vs. the Intensity rating. On a success, the target(s) are only knocked down. On a fail, the target(s) are pushed to back a number of meters equal to the points of failure, and knocked prone. Also, they fall damage equal to the distance pushed.

spells.name: Detect magic
spells.text: The caster can detect the presence of magic on items, creatures or other entities as they light up in different lustrous colors, depending on the source of the magic. The detection zone is equal to the blast zone. The caster gets a sense of the realm and power of the magic, but not the exact purpose, nature or effect of the magic.

spells.name: Lesser illusion
spells.text:
The caster molds and sculpts the streams of the Aether, to form an illusion, based on one of the five normal senses (sight, sound, feel, taste, smell).
Any target failing a Willpower save vs. the intensity of the spell, believes the illusion to be true. An illusion cannot, however, impact, affect, exert force or harm a creature, whether they believe it or not.

spells.name: Identify magic
spells.text: The caster is able to identify the effect of a number of magical effects equal to the intensity rating of the spell.

spells.name: Mind manipulation
spells.text: Character uses the magical streams to convince the target to perform one single suggested act. The action cannot be total foreign to the target, like killing himself, killing a loved one, a child, etc. Neither to commit treason or something that goes against his core religious or cultural beliefs. The target gets a Willpower save vs. the Intensity rating of the spell.

spells.name: Mind bomb
spells.text: The caster launches a spike of mental overload into the mind of the target. The target takes damage to his MP. The target is allowed a Willpower save vs. the intensity rating of the spell, adding any points of failure to the DMR.

spells.name: Dispel magic
spells.text: For a period of time, the caster can dismantle the effect of a spell. The targeted spell (the caster of the target spell) gets a Willpower save vs. the Intensity rating of this spell.

spells.name: Daze
spells.text: The caster manipulates the Aether to inflict a target with indecisiveness and mental haze. The target must pass a Willpower save vs. the intensity of the spell, or suffer one ‘Disorientation(x)’ instance for each 3 points of failure.

spells.name: Decipher
spells.text: The caster gains the ability to read and write any language for the duration of the spell.

spells.name: Invisibility
spells.text:
The caster and all items he wield, wear or hold (as part of his equipment) becomes invisible. The caster is considered ‘Hidden’ even when in line of sight.
While invisible the character still affect the physical world around him (e.g. making footprints in snow or sand, or knock over a vase or lamp). But he does not cast a shadow.

spells.name: Ghostform
spells.text: The caster takes on a ghost-like form, and can thus pass through any solid organic or inorganic material. The material must be of non-magical barrier. Magical barriers cannot be penetrated by this spell. The caster can pass through a number of meters equal to the zone variable, and/or stay imbedded in the material equal to the duration.

spells.name: Phantasmal grip
spells.text: The caster creates an invisible grip of force, causing the target to become 'Restrained' unless he passes a Willpower save vs. The intensity of the spell, or until the effect ends.

spells.name: Magic seal
spells.text: The caster creates a magical seal on a container or physical door - lockbox, pouch, chest, door, portcullis, etc. The container or door cannot be opened by natural means, only by the password determined by the caster. This seal doesn't prevent the item from being pried open or destroyed. It only disables normal opening or pick locking attempts. The DC of dispelling the seal is equal to the Intensity rating of this spell.

spells.name: Illusion
spells.text:
The caster molds and sculpts the streams of the Aether, to form an illusion, based on three of the five normal senses (sight, sound, feel, taste, smell).
Any target failing a Willpower save vs. the intensity of the spell, believes the illusion to be true. An illusion cannot, however, impact, affect, exert force or harm a creature, whether they believe it or not.

spells.name: Haste
spells.text: While under the effect of the spell, the target has a number of extra action equal to the intensity score.

spells.name: Porting
spells.text: The caster can create a portal, allowing him and allies to travel instantly from one destination to another. The destination must be a place the caster knows well, by spending no less than 6 months of almost daily activity in the place. Alternatively, create a binding stone, by impounding 15 MP to an object, serving as destination anchor. The Intensity rating defines the number of travelers that can pass through, before the portal closes.

spells.name: Implosion
spells.text: The caster creates a forcefield inside a target. The forcefield clutches the internal organs of the target, and starts crushing them with an implosive vacuum, bypassing any TOU bonus granted by wearing armor. The target must pass a Fortitude save vs. the intensity rating, or add any points of failure to the DMR.

spells.name: Mass daze
spells.text: The caster manipulates the Aether to inflict a group of targets with indecisiveness and mental haze. The targets must pass a Willpower save vs. the intensity of the spell, or suffer one ‘Disorientation(x)’ instance for each 3 points of failure.

spells.name: Uncanny linguist
spells.text: The caster gains the ability to speak any language for the duration of the spell.

spells.name: Greater illusion
spells.text:
The caster molds and sculpts the streams of the Aether, to form an illusion, based on all five of the normal senses (sight, sound, feel, taste, smell).
Any target failing a Willpower save vs. the intensity of the spell, believes the illusion to be true. An illusion cannot, however, impact, affect, excert force or harm a creature, if they believe it or not.

spells.name: Mind control
spells.text:
With the power of the Aether, the caster compels a target to follow any command of the caster, even attack allies, if the target fails his Willpower save vs. the intensity of the spell.
The target will, however, gain a secondary save with 2 advantages, if the command goes against the target's core beliefs like killing a loved one (e.g. one of their children), or any other core concept they base their life and identity on (GM's discretion).

spells.name: Time trance
spells.text: Tapping into the Aether, the caster can experience a playback of what has happened in the past, within the Burst zone. He can go back a number of days equal to the range. And he can hold focus (playback time) a number of minutes equal to the duration. He can scroll back and forth 6 hours (a 12 hour window), while he maintains focus. He can choose a number of sensory channels (visual, auditive, smell, feel, etc.) equal to the intensity rating.

spells.name: Reality distortion
spells.text:
The caster permeates the target with Aether energy, twisting the perception and senses of the target. If the target fails his Willpower save vs. the intensity of the spell, he believes the reality around him to be whatever the caster determines, for as long as the spell lasts.
The mental guile adapts to the surroundings, making them appear as part of the distortion, in whatever image is appropriate for the 'mental scenery'.

spells.name: Nightfall
spells.text: Caster creates a zone in which it becomes dark, as a starlit night. The zone is 2 meters in height. The darkness reacts as normal night and can be lit by normal means of light. The zone obstructs line of sight.
clarifications: House ruling: the text describes a zone, so 4/2 has been moved from burst to zone.

spells.name: Shadowbolt
spells.text: The caster conjures a bolt of cold, dark and whispering fog, that shoots at the target. The caster can imbue the shadow bolt with homing capabilities, by adding intensity points to the spell. For each intensity point, the spell has a +1 bonus to hit.

spells.name: Animate dead
spells.text: The caster can animate any dead within the burst zone. The animated corpses will have statistics equal to the ones they had while alive. The caster can only raise a creature of a character level equal to the caster himself + the intensity score of the spell. Through this spell, the caster also gains the ability to know, what level the intended target is.

spells.name: Vampiric drain
spells.text: As the caster reaches out, a string of translucent black fog springs from his hand. The target must make a Willpower save vs. the Intensity rating of the spell. The target looses a number of BP equal to the points of failure. Any BP lost by the target, is transferred to the caster. If the caster is at full health, he can gain a maximum number of additional temporary BP equal to his CHA score.

spells.name: Bloodfever
spells.text: With dark chants, the caster connects to the magical streams, manipulating them to make his target bleed from the eyes, ears, nose and mouth. The target must make a Fortitude save vs. the Intensity rating of the spell. If he fails, he suffers one instance of ‘Persistent Damage(x)’ bleed, for each 2 points of failure.

spells.name: Curse of the sinner
spells.text: Caster booms out a commanding voice, demanding each enemy in the blast zone to make a Willpower save vs. the Intensity rating of the spell. If they fail, they are burdened and tormented by remorse of sins, inflicting disadvantage to all skills checks (including attacks and spell casting), until the spell ends.

spells.name: Soul ripper
spells.text: The caster hurls a translucent soul image at a target. Before rolling the check to hit the target, the target rolls a Willpower save vs. the intensity of the spell. On a fail, the attack ignores all DFR and TOU bonus granted by non-magical armor, otherwise the armor protects at normal.

spells.name: Essence taint
spells.text: The caster focuses his mind on the immediate surroundings, and is able to channel the life essence out of nearby living creatures. All leeched life essence is transformed to MP to the caster. All non-willing targets in the burst is allowed a Willpower save vs. the Intensity rating of the spell. For each point of failure, the caster drains them of 1 MP.

spells.name: Foul summons
spells.text: The caster uses the Aether to reach the realms beyond, summoning a demon to do his bidding. The caster can command the demon from the next round, as an action. The Demon's stats are: BP: Equal to the caster's max MP; Melee skill is 5 + caster's level; DFR 12 + caster's level; TOU equals Intensity rating; Melee DMR equal to spell DMR; Movement rate equal to zone. The demon perishes on a critical hit.

spells.name: Bloodcraze
spells.text: By channeling the magical streams, the caster places crazy thoughts in the mind of his target, making the target turn into a total and mindless frenzy if he fails his Willpower save vs. the spell's Intensity rating. The victim will attack the nearest possible target. If more targets are adjacent, they must roll luck to see who gets attacked. If none are adjacent, the target will run up to the nearest, using any BP needed to get there and attack.

spells.name: Mind terror
spells.text: The caster emits a terrifying sensation in his immediate vicinity. Any enemy caught in the zone must make a Willpower save vs. the Intensity rating of the spell. Anyone failing, will be ‘Stunned(x)’ by fear, a number of instances equal to their points of failure.

spells.name: Blood sacrifice
spells.text: With dark chants, the caster contaminates an areas with tainted Aether, manipulating every target in the area to bleed from the eyes, ears, nose and mouth. The target(s) must make a Fortitude save vs. the Intensity rating of the spell. If he fails, he suffers one instance of ‘Persistent Damage(x)’ bleed, for each 2 points of failure.

spells.name: Condemned
spells.text:
Woven into dark chants and aggressive gestures, the caster diminishes the essence of a target for a brief moment, by condemning it.
If the target fails a Willpower save vs. the intensity rating of the spell, the target becomes ‘Weakened’, ‘Off-guard’ and ‘Disoriented(2)’ for the duration of the spell.

spells.name: Deep dark
spells.text: Caster creates a zone of pitch-black magical darkness. This darkness cannot be illuminated by normal means of light. The caster is immune to the darkness, and can see under the natural circumstances in the zone. This magical darkness also hinders creatures that have normal abilities to see in darkness. Only 'True light' can illuminate this type of darkness.

spells.name: Mist of doom
spells.text: The caster shrouds himself in a dark mist. Any enemies within the zone must make a Willpower save vs. the Intensity rating of the spell. On a fail, the target is cursed and loose 1 CON score point for each 5 points of failure, until the curse is cured.

spells.name: Bone brittle
spells.text: With an ominous command, the caster manipulates the magical streams to crush the bones of his enemy. The target must make a Fortitude save vs. The Intensity rating of the spell. If the target fails his save, he suffers 1 wound.

spells.name: Call of darkness
spells.text:
The caster uses the Aether to reach the realms beyond, summoning a demon to do his bidding. The caster can command the demon from the next round, as an action. The Demon's stats are: BP: Equal to twice the caster's max MP; Melee skill is 5 + caster's level; DFR 12 + caster's level; TOU equals Intensity; Melee DMR equal to spell DMR; Movement rate equal to zone.
  GameMastering RGA Running the game If you are familiar with other tabletop roleplaying games, running a game of RuneGate shouldn’t be that di erent.
Even so, there are many tips, tricks and ways to go about it that helps your role as a GameMaster (GM). Most of these will, however, be covered in the GameMaster’s supplement.
This section of the book is meant for you, the GM, to understand some of the areas where RuneGate might stand out, and how to handle it.
Action, adventure, tension RuneGate is meant to be a game of great fun, enjoyment and action. The game is designed with action movies and fast-paced gameplay in mind. Think, Marvel® movies, Mission: Impossible®, Harry Potter® and narrative universes alike.
That is not to say, the game cannot support more gritty setting like Lord of the Rings®, Game of Thrones® and The Witcher® – it can.
But the game mechanics have been deliberately designed to support fast - yet deep - forward-moving gameplay.
Fail forward One of the carrying elements to support this is the fail forward philosophy. Running over the Skill check result guideline table should support the impression that failure shouldn’t happen too often, and never regarding elements of the game that could potentially grind the narrative and plot to a halt.
However, successes with complications, raising the stakes, introducing more tension to the story, makes up great stories and fun, memorable game sessions.
Much more on this topic, can be found in the GM Supplement.
Adjust at own behest We hope you will find the mechanics supporting the type of roleplaying game experience you like and prefer. But never should you let any of the mechanics and rules get in the way of your preferred playstyle and how you enjoy playing the game.
The system is meant as a framework, and if anything comes in the way of how you want to run or adjudicate the came – change it, add to it, and maybe even give us feedback. RuneGate is much more than a fixed set of rules, if anything, we encourage you to join the discussions about the game and rules. Your feedback might be the one leading to changes, fixes, updates and adjustments.
GameMastering RuneGate  We would like to see RuneGate as a “living organism”, changing over time, into something better all the time. For this, you can join our online community at www.thisisthemostawesomewebaddressever.com.
Consequences of Actions One of the most important aspects of creating stories is the ever-present conflict.
Conflict is usually introduced through challenges and obstacles that cannot be easily overcome or are achieved at some cost to the protagonist. Great stories revolve around the fact that every action, or at least most actions, have consequences to make things interesting.
As a GM, you should consider that whenever you ask a player to roll their dice, the outcome of the roll—whether it's a save or some sort of skill check—should have consequences. But it's not just about rolling dice; decisions made in the game should also have consequences. These consequences can come in a wide range of types and e ects, such as losing Body Points or Mind Points (as explained in the skill chapter). They can also include added complications to the narrative, misuse or extra use of time, or depletion of resources that the character might have or that are scarce in the story you're telling.
All of these consequences are crucial for bringing tension into the game. Tension keeps your players on the edge of their seats and enhances their enjoyment of the story you're creating together.
Consequences and tension might jeopardize relationships with NPCs or even between the players. They might a ect the players' relationships with the region or create an increasing number of complications in achieving their goals.
These considerations are integrated into the mechanics of RuneGate, but it's your job as the GM, along with your players, to enforce this feeling when telling your collaborative story together.
Many of these topics will be elaborated in the GameMaster’s Supplement.
Conditions Many cases, situations, e ects, spells, skills etc. apply or cause a range of di erent conditions in the game. These conditions have game mechanical meaning for the target(s) subjected to the e ect. Below is the collection of conditions in RuneGate, and how they a ect a target.
Blinded You can’t see, rendering you unable to use vision as a precise sense, and su er three disadvantages to all Perception & Awareness checks.
All targets become ‘Hidden’ from you, and you become ‘O -guard’ to them.
Lastly, all terrain is considered di cult terrain, since moving too fast risk you falling.
 Concealed means the character is di cult to clearly see, maybe due to standing in fog, smoke, heavy rain or foliage. If targeted by an attack, the attacker must pass a DC 5 flat check, otherwise the attack is an automatic miss. Otherwise, the attacker rolls a normal attack roll.
Constrained means you’re pinned down and have great di culty moving. You’re ‘Immobile’ and ‘O -Guard’. You cannot take actions, other than an action attempting to break free from this condition.
Dazed(x) As ‘Disorientation’. However, the condition and following penalty only ends when the condition ends.
Trying to perform actions with the ‘Concentration’ trait (e.g. spell casting), the target must pass a DC 5 flat check or loose the action without e ect.
Disoriented(x) Target has a status penalty to skill checks, including attacks and spell casting equal to the number of instances of ‘Disorientation’. Each time the target takes an action, on his own turn, the ‘Disorientation’ condition drops 1 instance.
Trying to perform actions with the ‘Concentration’ trait (e.g. spell casting), the target must pass a DC 5 flat check, or loose the action without e ect.
Dying(x) When having the ‘Dying’ condition, at the start of his turn, the only available action is for the character to make a flat check with a DC 10 + the number of wounds the character has accrued.
Failing the save with 1-9 points, means the character accrues an additional wound.
Failing with 10 or more points, means the character accrues 2 additional wounds.
Succeeding the check means the character stabilizes, lying on the ground unconscious.
If the combined number of wounds reaches the character’s total Wound Threshold, the character dies.
This process proceeds until the character is stabilized.
Notice! If a character takes any damage, while ‘Dying’, he receives and additional ‘Wounded(x)’ condition.
Frightened(x) While being ‘Frightened(x)’, the target takes a circumstance penalty, equal to the (x) for all checks regarding skills, combat, defenses, saves and spell casting. Also, his Hero DC is lowered by the same penalty.
Critically failing a check of this sort also means the target will spend its next (x) actions moving half its speed away from the source of the fear.
Grabbed means you’re ‘Immobile’, ‘O -Guard’. If you try to take actions (e.g.

 Hidden means a creature cannot be easily perceived by other creatures, especially if sight is the only precise sense the perceiving creature has (e.g. being invisible or hiding behind a curtain). Depending on the circumstances, ‘Hidden’ creatures can still be attacked, but the attacker must roll a DC 10 flat check. On a failure, the attack automatically misses, otherwise the attacker can roll a normal attack roll.
Attacking a creature, while being ‘Hidden’ grants a +4 conditional modifier to the attack roll. Often, an attack ends the ‘Hidden’ condition, but it is up to the GM’s discretion.
Immobile means the character’s SPD drops to 0, while inflicted with the ‘Immobile’ condition.
Infected(x) The character is infected by an ailment, substance, toxin, poison, disease or reagent that reduces his ability to perform. While ‘Infected’, the character has a condition penalty to all checks, including saves and defenses equal to the number of instances of ‘Infected’.
The e ects last until the condition is removed/saved against.
O -guard You’re not able to fully defend yourself. Attackers have advantages to hit you, while you’re o -guard.

All skill- and attribute checks for INT, WIS and CHA, as well as saves are done with a penalty equal to the number of ‘Mind-dull’ instances.
Moreover, the character also su ers an equal damage penalty for all attacks based on either INT, WIS or CHA.

Persistent Damage(x) is a condition that forces the character to take damage at the beginning of his turn, equal to the “x” value of the condition.
The character is allowed a DC 11 flat check at the end of his turn (the round after being subjected), to reduce the condition 2 points of “x”.
Prone You are on the ground, flat. While being ‘Prone’, you are also ‘O -guard’ to melee attacks, but have ‘Cover’ against ranged attacks.
You have disadvantage to all attack and spell casting checks.
Resistance(x) means the character has a resistance against damage or e ects from one or more types. If it is a damage resistance, the “x” represents how many points of inflicted damage is reduced, before applied to the character.
If it is resistance to an e ect, the “x” represents the bonus the character has for saving throws against the e ect.
 Rooted(x) You gain a SPD penalty equal to the value of the condition, until the condition ends.

Unaware means the creature does not know about the incoming attack and thus cannot defend themselves in any fashion. While ‘Unaware’ against an attack, the creature cannot apply his DEX to his DFR, and is only allowed to use half his skill bonus.
DFR calculation for ‘Unaware’ targets becomes: 8 + Armor bonus + Half skill bonus.
Undetected means you’re not perceived by other creatures. They do not know about your presence, and must act accordingly.
If attacking another creature, while being ‘Undetected’, the targeted creature is considered ‘Unaware’. Attacking while being ‘Undetected’ ends the condition, and allows you to become ‘Hidden’ in the best case, or maybe entirely revealed to the target. It all depends on the circumstance but is at the GM’s discretion.
Vulnerable(x) means the character is especially susceptible to damage or e ects from one or more types. If it is a damage vulnerability, the “x” represents how many extra points of inflicted damage is added, before applied to the character.
If it is vulnerability to an e ect, the “x” represents the penalty the character has for saving throws against the e ect.
Weakened(x) means the character has been drained of might and power, losing energy and ability to e ectively perform physically.
All skill- and attribute checks for STR, CON and DEX, as well as saves are done with a penalty equal to the number of ‘Weakened’ instances.
Moreover, the character also su er an equal damage penalty for all attacks based on either STR, CON or DEX.
 Wounded(x) means the character sustains an injury of such severity it hinders him until it is healed or mended. Also, and more importantly, if a character reaches a number of wounds equal to his Wound threshold he drops dead.
Each instance of the Wounded condition inflicts -1 penalty on all skill checks.
 Rest and recovery Base Recovery When adventurers explore the wild and uncanny world, they eventually become exhausted, injured in combat, by accidents, traps, etc.
Healing up wounds takes time, treatment, good nutrition and rest!
Circumstances surrounding a character’s recovery greatly a ect his ability to recover.
Usually, a character gains his Recovery Points (RP) one time each day, after 8 hours of rest, whereas 6 of them must be spent sleeping. He gains a number of RP equal to his Constitution score + CON.
Many things may grant additional recovery points (RP), like good food, decent resting conditions, mild weather, sleep, entertainment, attendance by a professional medic etc.
Once the contribution of the various sources has been determined the additional points of RP are added to the base RP.
Regaining BP and MP Body Points and Mind Points don’t regenerate by themselves, only during rest.
However, it does demand rest for it to happen.
The body and mind restore, when the character rests along with eating, drinking and other leisure.
A single regained BP or MP costs 1 Recovery Point. Each must be bought separately.
E.g. For 7 recovery points, the player can for instance restore 4 BP and 3 MP, or 7 MP. He can mix it anyway he wants.
Mending wounds Wounds sustained from critical hits or falling prone, dying, are more grave than superficial injuries and scratches.
A wound takes 25 recovery points to remove.
See the Medical & Care skill on, how a trained physician can aid the recovery of wounds, without a character spending as much RP on it himself.
Disease / Poison Recovering from either disease or poisoning may be a tiresome a air. The character is allowed a new save against the ailment for 5 recovery points, but only one save per day.
 Sources of additional recovery Food and drink Food and drink are one of the primary sources of recovery from injuries and ailments. However, food and drink come in a wide variety of quality and standards, and the better the food and drink, the better the recovery e ects.
Most standard meals simply keep the character well-fed and nourished. However, better food and beverages might grant special recovery bonuses or e ects.
Medical aid Medical aid helps a great deal, when you’re injured or subjected to mysterious ailments from alien planets or creatures. Refer to the Medical & Care skill on how this aids recovery.
Entertainment Nothing like a great tale, pleasant song or lovely melody to lift morale, and aid recovery. In general characters able to make performances lift the spirits in a camp, and on the road. The GM might also determine that some types of gambling and games can contribute to the overall recovery bonus.
A character can add a conditional modifier to recovery, with a performance check (singing, music, tale telling, playing games etc.). Thus, a result of 15 grants +2, 20 grants +5, 25 grants +10 and 30 grants +20. A character is allowed one attempt per day, to aid the groups recovery check.
At GM’s discretion the same old stories, melodies and songs may wear thin, and new a repertoire must be learned to keep a band or fellowship in high spirits.
Moreover, the GM might decide that the party can only benefit from songs and music from one character, thus three characters playing and singing only count as one collective performance. This way, one character may sing and play, and another tells great stories to benefit from multiple sources of entertainment.
Sources of exhaustion Travelling Travelling does no good for people trying to relax, rest or recover. Especially not if travelling on foot. Only larger vehicles grant restoration during travel, since some resting can be performed at the backseat of a long-distance coach, carriage or wagon. More luxurious versions are seen, but considered uncommon, and mainly for the wealthy.
It is up to the GM to assess what the general activity level, while travelling, is for the character. Travelling for 1 hour, then bustling around a city may not qualify as travelling.
 Weather conditions One of the primary causes of demoralization, death, degeneration, disease, infections and other ailments is bad weather. Travelling in the wild or hostile environments is bad for recovery and may drain the spirits of most people. Bad weather is generally bad for recovery. Weather e ects also stack, meaning stormy weather, heavy rain, lightnings crackling and thunder rolling, will collectively decrease recovery options than just a light rain.
 Enemies and Adversaries One of the central parts of conflict and consequence is the presence of combat and battle in any tabletop roleplaying game. RuneGate is not very di erent in this regard. While it can be compared to many other tabletop roleplaying games, you might have tried, there are a few di erences in how you should manage, handle, and operate monsters, creatures, enemies, and adversaries in RuneGate. In this game, all NPCs, adversaries, monsters, or creatures come in one of four di erent classes: Minions, Standard, Elite, and Villains. Each class has specific attributes that a ect how you can and should play them as a GM.
Minions Minions are your typical cannon fodder enemies. This doesn't necessarily mean that minions are weak; they have the same stats, skills, and attributes as an equivalent creature of the same type in another class. The key di erence is that minions have only a single BP, so whenever a minion is struck in combat, it is defeated.
Another special feature of minions is that they can assemble into what is called minion groups. This means that a selection of minions can act together as a single entity in combat, with only a single turn during the encounter. When you attack a minion group, you reduce the group by one minion for each successful hit. The minion group has the same stats as the individual minions but acts as a single entity in combat.
The special feature of bundling minions into minion groups is that for every two minions in the group beyond the first one, the group attacks with an advantage. For example, three minions bundled together in a group will attack with one advantage, while five minions bundled together will attack with two advantages, and so on and so forth.
As a measurement of challenge, you can roughly play 3 Minions per player character.
Standard Standard class mobs are not that dissimilar to minions. They have the same stats, attributes, skills, and abilities; however, they cannot be bundled into groups. The key di erence compared to minions is that, Standard enemies have full amount of Body Points but, if the standard creature receives a critical hit the creature is instantly defeated. This makes standard creatures a bit more resilient than the average minion and therefore a bit more of a challenge.
As a measurement of challenge, you can roughly play 2 Standard creatures for 1 player character.
 Elite Elite creatures are among the toughest and most resilient of all creature classes that an adventuring party can encounter. In every aspect, an elite creature is like a player character. It has a comparable amount of Body Points, Mind Points and stats as a fully fleshed-out player character. This means that an elite creature of the same level and power would constitute a one-to-one threat to an individual character.
As a rule of thumb, you could consider a ratio of 1 Elite class creatures to 1player character.
Villain Villain class creatures are extraordinary adversaries, possessing powers that lie beyond those of normal creatures and even normal characters. These creatures enjoy a range of bonuses, making them tougher and more resilient than any other creatures of the same type. Villain class creatures are rarer and shouldn't be used in every encounter. They should be reserved for special occasions where the adventuring party meets a significant villain, boss, or reaches a crucial crossroad in the story you are telling together.
Besides having an elevated range of attributes and stats compared to normal creatures, Villain creatures should also be played with tactical prowess, using the same options and mechanical functions as the players. This means using movement, flanking, strategies etc., constituting an even greater threat than a normal creature.
In many cases, as a GM, you might also accompany the villain creature with other creatures of the same or di erent type but with di erent classes.
In many cases, you should most likely consider, also making a villain class creature 1-2 levels higher than the adventuring party characters.
A Villain class creature roughly roughly challenges 2-3 player characters.
Large and huge creatures Even though large and huge creatures are not individual classes like the ones mentioned above, there are important considerations when handling and playing them in RuneGate. Large and huge creatures are meant to be real threats, not just another creature that the adventuring party can hammer aimlessly upon until it passes out. These creatures are dangerous and di cult to overcome because their mere presence and movement on the battlefield pose a threat to those surrounding them.
In general, large and huge creatures are considered an encounter all by themselves.
A large creature is considered equal to four elite type creatures, and a huge creature is considered equal to seven to eight elite creatures. When controlling a large or huge creature, you should play them ferociously and with a tactical mindset.
Most large and huge creatures also have increased speed, a higher number of hit points, increased toughness, and improved physical saves, making them a  tremendous threat to an adventuring party of four to five players. On top of this, many large and huge creatures use natural attacks equivalent to player-character unarmed attacks. This means that many of their attacks have Fast(5) or Fast(10) property on their natural attacks, such as claws, bites, tail-bashes and similar types.
When controlling a large creature, be mindful that it not only does more damage and survives longer, but also has abilities and properties described in its characteristics that make it dangerous just by moving around the battlefield.
